what_was_judged: the eight outline entries against bible/world.md ## Rules. No draft existed; this judges the commission.
violations_note: No beat orders an event the rules forbid. Chapter 5 beat 2 — Hale deliberately leaving the theodolite out overnight — was examined and is drama, not a defect: a character breaking a custom on purpose is what the rule exists to be told through.

ambiguous_rules.issue: whose measurement is it — the hand on the chain or the hand in the book?
ambiguous_rules.arbitration: accepted. Fowler leads the chain on both the Day 2 line and the Day 6 re-run; under the chainman reading those two figures must be identical, which the outline contradicts, and Chapter 3 beat 3 becomes unexplained. The surveyor-of-record reading makes every beat consistent.
ambiguous_rules.applied: R1 rewritten to name the surveyor of record — the hand that wrote it in the field book — and to exclude whoever held the chain under their direction.

ambiguous_rules.issue: after leaving and returning, do repeats differ once and then stabilise, or never repeat again?
ambiguous_rules.arbitration: ambiguity accepted, the critic's proposed fix OVERRULED. The critic wrote out the one-time-shift reading, which contradicts Chapter 4 beat 4 (three more runs, three more figures) and the Chapter 4 plant ('nothing he re-measures will ever repeat again'). Chapter 8 beat 4 does not need stability to return: the columns sum twice alike there because the triangulation is rebuilt on the three constants of R2, not because Hale's own lines started repeating. A replacement built on the critic's reading would have written the error into six chapters by hand.
ambiguous_rules.applied: R1 rewritten to the permanent reading: once the surveyor of record has gone out and come back, that line never repeats for them again and every fresh attempt differs from the last.

ambiguous_rules.issue: does R2 guarantee only that each constant measures the same, or that angles between them close?
ambiguous_rules.arbitration: accepted. Both beats need the stronger reading and the book's resolution rests on it entirely.
ambiguous_rules.applied: R2 rewritten to state that the three measure the same singly and in relation to one another, and that angles and distances taken directly among them close identically whatever lies between.

ambiguous_rules.issue: is 'no instrument stands after sunset' a physical law or a custom? And is Raven Hause's light the clock everywhere, or only at Raven Hause?
ambiguous_rules.arbitration: accepted on both clauses. As written the first sentence reads as an absolute the dale enforces, which would make Chapter 5 beat 2 impossible rather than transgressive; and Chapter 8 beat 3 takes an entry at the Raven Hause station 'with the light still on the fell', which needs the clock stated.
ambiguous_rules.applied: R5 rewritten: leaving an instrument out is a thing no local does, not a thing the dale prevents; the theodolite stands where it was put; the light off Raven Hause is the dale's dusk everywhere in the dale at once, and no local signs at any station between dusk and dawn.

ambiguous_rules.issue: does the prohibition cover reading a distance aloud from a page, as against speaking one?
ambiguous_rules.arbitration: accepted. Chapter 8 beat 1 has Dent read the perambulation book aloud to the whole dale and the chapter cannot be written without knowing whether that is lawful.
ambiguous_rules.applied: R4 rewritten to cover reading off a page as well as speaking, with the structural consequence stated: nothing dale-born hands have written contains a distance to read, which is why the perambulation book keeps the bound in durations and dead men's names.

ambiguous_rules.issue: does a correction inherit the original entry's witnesses, or need two of its own?
ambiguous_rules.arbitration: accepted, though 'of its own' already favours the second reading. This is the exact rule that deadlocked a previous run of this pipeline, and it is the load-bearing constraint of the whole ending. Making it explicit costs one clause.
ambiguous_rules.applied: R3 rewritten: a correction is a new entry in every respect, needing two witnesses who stood at that station for the taking of the correction itself; the original's witnesses count for nothing toward it even if they are the same two people.

outcome: bible/world.md ## Rules rewritten before FLOW-4. Six rules in, six rules out — none added, none removed, no beat changed. The outline was not re-dispatched because no beat was unlawful.
